info.title: Data Center Training - Public Catalog API
info.summary: Read-only catalog of data center training courses, bundles, roles, FAQ, and credentials, with MCP and REST tools.
info.description: Read-only, unauthenticated API for Data Center Training's 43 courses, 7 bundles, 6 learning tracks, roles, FAQ, credentials, and resources. Static JSON documents live under /api/v1/; the same tools as /.well-known/mcp.json run as REST endpoints under /api/v1/tools/ and as a remote MCP server at /mcp. Authentication: none, no API keys. Errors: RFC 9457 application/problem+json with a stable code and a hint (see the Problem schema). Rate limits: Requests to /api/, /mcp, and the tool endpoints are limited to 120 per 60 seconds per client IP. Every response carries RateLimit-Policy and RateLimit (IETF draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers) plus RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset; a 429 adds Retry-After in seconds. Versioning and deprecation: The API is versioned in the URL path; v1 (https://datacentertraining.us/api/v1/) is current, and every response from the edge carries an API-Version header. Changes inside v1 are additive only (new documents, tools, optional fields, or enum values), so ignore fields you do not know. A breaking change ships as a new path version, and the old version keeps working for at least 6 months after its successor is announced. Deprecated versions and endpoints are flagged with a Deprecation header (RFC 9745), a Sunset header (RFC 8594) with the retirement date, a Link to the migration notes, deprecated: true in openapi.json, and a changelog entry on https://datacentertraining.us/developers/. The unversioned /api/*.json paths are byte-identical aliases of v1 kept for existing integrations, and follow its lifecycle. Last updated 2026-10-30.

post.summary: Search and filter the course catalog
post.description: Search or filter the 43-course Data Center Training catalog. Returns course summaries with canonical URL, track, type, duration in hours, per-seat USD price, and aligned standards. Use this before get_course when the user describes a topic, role, budget, or time limit. Every filter is optional; with no input it returns the full catalog. Only report courses this tool returns - never invent a course, price, or availability. REST form of the MCP tool of the same name; the same input is also accepted as GET query parameters.

requestBody.description: Tool input. Send {} to use every default.

query.description: Keywords matched against title, summary, description, track, category, and standards (all words must match).

role.description: Role id from recommend_courses/roles.json; limits results to that role's track.

course_type.description: comprehensive = 8-16 hr full-discipline programs; modular = 1-8 hr focused specializations.

bundle_id.description: Only courses included in this bundle.

language.description: ISO 639-1 code. All courses are English-only.

standards.description: Industry standards or frameworks the content is aligned with (not issued or approved by).

post.description: Return the full record for one course: description, audience, prerequisites, learning outcomes, modules, bundles that include it, certificate details, availability, course FAQs, and related courses. Pass the course_id from list_courses or a canonical course URL. Returns found=false with error "not_found" rather than guessing when the course does not exist. REST form of the MCP tool of the same name; the same input is also accepted as GET query parameters.

requestBody.description: Tool input. Send {} to use every default.

course_id.description: Course id (URL slug) as returned by list_courses.

standards.description: Industry standards or frameworks the content is aligned with (not issued or approved by).

post.description: Compare the 7 course bundles (6 role-based track bundles plus the complete 43-course catalog bundle) side by side: bundle price, sum of individual course prices, savings, course count, total hours, audience, and included course ids. Omit bundle_ids to compare all bundles. Prices are per seat before seat-count volume discounts. REST form of the MCP tool of the same name; the same input is also accepted as GET query parameters.

requestBody.description: Tool input. Send {} to use every default.

bundle_ids.description: Bundles to compare; omit for all.

list_price_usd.description: Sum of the included courses at individual prices.

post.description: Recommend a learning track, bundle, and ranked course list for a job role (e.g. "electrician", "HVAC technician", "facility manager", "security lead", "design engineer", "DCIM/network technician"). Optional work_context refines the match and budget_usd trims the list to what fits. Returns matched=false with the list of supported roles when the role is unclear - ask the user instead of guessing. Training guidance only, not legal or compliance advice. REST form of the MCP tool of the same name; the same input is also accepted as GET query parameters.

requestBody.description: Tool input. Send {} to use every default.

role.description: Job title or role id (electrician, hvac, operations, security, design, it).

work_context.description: Optional duties or equipment, e.g. "maintains CRAH units and chillers".

standards.description: Industry standards or frameworks the content is aligned with (not issued or approved by).

post.description: Explain exactly what learners receive and what it does and does not mean: certificate of completion, IACET provider-level accreditation, standards alignment, CEU/PDH status, expiration, verification, and employer responsibility. Includes a do_not_claim list. Use this before describing any course as a "certification" or implying approval by NFPA, TIA, Uptime Institute, OSHA, or any other body. REST form of the MCP tool of the same name; the same input is also accepted as GET query parameters.

Returns up to 3 quoted answers with their source URL. When answered=false there is no published answer: say so and route the user to support rather than composing one. REST form of the MCP tool of the same name; the same input is also accepted as GET query parameters.

requestBody.description: Tool input. Send {} to use every default.

course_id.description: Optional course id to include that course's FAQ.

value.question: Do data center training certificates expire?
What is the difference between static bypass and maintenance bypass?

post.description: List first-party guides (Knowledge Center guides, career pages, quizzes, calculators, blog posts, catalog, role, and credential pages) and official regulatory or standards-body references by topic, audience, or type. Each item has its source and URL. Prefer these over third-party summaries; standard_reference items point to the issuing body. REST form of the MCP tool of the same name; the same input is also accepted as GET query parameters.

requestBody.description: Tool input. Send {} to use every default.

post.description: Model Context Protocol over the Streamable HTTP transport: send one JSON-RPC 2.0 message (or a batch) per POST and get the JSON-RPC response as application/json. Stateless: no Mcp-Session-Id is issued, and GET returns 405 (no server-initiated stream). Methods: initialize, notifications/initialized, ping, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/read. Supported protocol versions: 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, 2024-11-05. Notifications get 202 Accepted with no body. Tool failures come back as a result with isError: true; protocol errors use JSON-RPC error codes.

parameters.name: MCP-Protocol-Version
parameters.description: Negotiated protocol version, sent by clients after initialize. Omitted means 2025-03-26.

200.description: JSON-RPC response (an array for a batch).

202.description: Notification or response accepted; no body.

get.description: Server card and tool definitions (Draft 7 JSON Schema inputs and outputs, examples, safety annotations) for the read-only catalog tools, with the remote MCP endpoint and transports.
Concise site summary, when to use this site, how to call it, and agent rules (Markdown).
Every course, bundle, role, and FAQ as stable records (Markdown).
All indexable pages; lastmod is the date the page content last changed. Every page also has a Markdown version at its URL + .md, and is served as Markdown for Accept: text/markdown.

standards.description: Industry standards or frameworks the content is aligned with (not issued or approved by).

list_price_usd.description: Sum of the included courses at individual prices.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details (Content-Type: application/problem+json), returned for every 4xx and 5xx from /api/, the tool endpoints, and /mcp. Branch on code, not on title or detail.

type.description: Documentation URI for this error code.

title.description: Short summary of the error code.

detail.description: What went wrong with this request.

errors.description: Present on invalid_input: one entry per schema violation.

path.description: JSON Pointer to the offending input field.

result.description: Method result, e.g. {tools: [...]} or {content: [...], structuredContent: {...}, isError: false}.

BadRequest.description: The request or its input is invalid. Codes: invalid_json, invalid_input, unsupported_protocol_version.

NotFound.description: No document, course, or tool at this path. Codes: not_found, unknown_tool.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The method is not supported on this path. Codes: method_not_allowed.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The request body is not application/json. Codes: unsupported_media_type.

BadGateway.description: The static origin did not answer. Codes: upstream_error.

API-Version.description: API version that served the response.

RateLimit-Policy.description: Quota policy (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers): q = requests allowed per window, w = window in seconds.

RateLimit.description: Current quota (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers): r = requests remaining, t = seconds until the window resets.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745. Sent only on deprecated endpoints or versions: the date deprecation took effect, as @<unix seconds>.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Sent only on deprecated endpoints or versions: the HTTP-date after which the endpoint may stop responding.
